headline: Approved June 17 and July 8 meeting minutes; heard Sierra Club presentation on clean energy and utility bills.
summary: The Climate Action & Sustainability Commission approved past meeting minutes, heard a Sierra Club presentation on clean energy and utility bill affordability, and discussed the Energy Coach Program memo and upcoming Empower funding. The group also reviewed project updates including the Bloomberg YCAF grant, Wicked Cool Mystic project, the annual progress report, and communication planning, and set the next meeting for September 9.
decisions: Approved the minutes from the June 17 and July 8 meetings unanimously.

decision_evidence.quote: Bob motioned to approve both sets of minutes. Amanda seconded and the motion was approved unanimously.

Clean energy and utility bills.

# City of Malden

# Climate Action & Sustainability Commission Agenda

| Tuesday, August 25, 2026 | 5:30PM | City Hall Room 113 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| | | 215 Pleasant Street |
| | | Malden, MA 02148 |

## Roll Call (1 min)

- Councilor Carey McDonald - Absent
- Staff Liaison Rebekah McPheeters - Present
- Diego Maldonado* (Secretary) - Absent
- Bob FitzPatrick* - Present
- Rachel Surrette* - Present
- Lipin Ji* - Present (virtually)
- Amanda Treat* (Vice Chair) - Present
- Ricky Ma* (Chair) - Present
- Vickash Mohanka from Seirra Club was present
- Julia Nassar from MAPC was present (virtually)

Ricky called the meeting to order at 5:35PM.

## Minutes to be Approved (4 min)

Commission to approve minutes from June 17 and July 8 meetings.

- Bob motioned to approve both sets of minutes. Amanda seconded and the motion was approved unanimously.

## Sierra Club (Vickash Mohanka, 20 min)

Clean energy and utility bills.

- Vick noted that in recent years, affordability has been seen as the best talking point for clean energy (i.e., lower your energy bill by switching to a municipal aggregation program), however, polling in New England shows that we can talk about affordability alongside climate and public health
- Because utility bill costs have increased dramatically, this is polling as a major issue for New England
- Utility companies in MA see a return on the amount of assets they own, so they are incentivized to own valuable assets
- The Future of Heat Initiative is encouraging the DPU to regulate utilities more
- Sierra Club is using story telling to advocate to elected about reducing the energy burden on residents, because in general, residents are paying more money for less gas (see: https://www.sierraclub.org/massachusetts/energy-burden)
- Sierra Club's stance is that we cannot invest in both clean energy and gas line replacement
- Sierra Club is advocating for batteries so that our grid can store more energy
- Sierra Club is also doing organizing work related to data centers
  - Malden has a moratorium on data centers
- Call to Action: Vick recommended that the CASC reach out to our reps about the energy bills that are in conference committee (H.5175), to advocate for
  - Restoring the Mass Save budget
  - Not changing the Alternative Compliance Payments (APCs)
  - Allowing residents to self-attest their income for Mass Save eligibility

Q&A.

- CASC requested to see the polling data & Sierra Club literature that Vick referenced

## Energy Coach Program Memo (10 min)

Feedback, questions & comments. (Ricky)

- CASC homework is to review the memo, Bekah will send out the link.

Next steps. (Julia)

- There will be a new round of Empower funding this fall. Julia will help us think through an application for energy coaching program, and we can also think about pairing this work with a HEAT SMART campaign.
- Note that this application will be Julia's final deliverable and her time with us will end after that.

## Project Updates & Announcements (15 min)

New CASC members. (Bekah)

- Ron Cochran resigned from CASC, and we have a new CASC member who will get appointed this fall
- We also have two new youth members that Ricky will reach out to

Bloomberg YCAF grant update. (Bekah)

- We published our open call and we have community partner orgs on board
- We are looking for opportunities to speak with Malden youth about the program (i.e., Back to School nights, club fairs, etc.)
- Timeline: Applications due 9/30, select winners in October, disperse funds by November, projects end by 4/15

Wicked Cool Mystic update. (Bekah)

- Wicked Cool Mystic skate park project wrapped & got good press
- Wicked Cool Mystic III MVP application was rejected, but Bekah is looking for other ways to continue the work of small scale cooling projects
- Ricky suggested we make sure that this kind of work is included in the City's new comprehensive plan

## General Comms & Annual Progress Report (Ricky, 20 min)

Final feedback/review of annual progress report.

- Change the Northern Strand photo (Bob will find a good picture)
- Generally, the CASC is happy with the format
- CASC to review on their own time, put comments in the shared deck, and let Bekah know when their comments are in

Next Steps: Deadline for comments 8/26, comms & translation plan.

- Ricky said the new deadline for comments is Friday 9/4
- Ricky and Lipin offered to handle the Chinese translation
- Bekah to get a new translation quote

Communication planning for CASC updates, tabling materials.

- Ricky noted it would be great to have standardized materials and messaging for tabling
- Suggested materials to use/create
  - QR code for the newsletter
  - CAP
  - Annual report
  - Flyers for programs we are promoting (Malden Community Electricity, etc.)
  - Elevator pitch
- Bekah to make a folder in SharePoint for this

Volunteer for August CASC newsletter.

- Amanda is back from vacation and can write it. Topics to include:
  - YCAF
  - Tease the report
  - Back to school "no idling" tip
  - Sierra Club update
  - Energy bill clinic 9/3 at MPL 4-7PM
  - Safe routes to school "Walking Weds" and "bike bus"

## Retrospective (Ricky, 10 min)

Recap Year One goals, progress, successes. (Ricky)

CASC Working Group Retrospective FY26.pptx (Ricky)

- Group decided we should do this retrospective together in our next meeting, Ricky will email it out

## Next Steps (5 min)

Discuss agenda for next meeting.

- Sierra Club debrief/potential action (consider inviting Grace Tumavicus from OSPCD to discuss)
- Consider MyWRA's CLEANAIR presentation, Black Earth Compost (Tabled)
- Youth member should be present at the next meeting, Ricky to reach out

Confirm date/time for next meeting.

- Wednesday, September 9 at 5:30PM

Share out any upcoming relevant events.

- We may need volunteers to pop up to promote YCAF
  - Ricky is available weekends and evenings
  - Bekah to send out the calls via email

## Adjournment – 7:00PM

- Bob motioned to adjourn, Rachel seconded. The meeting was adjourned at 7:11PM.
